title: Local model through a vendor CLI
lead: *Proposed:* let a role run on the owner's local vLLM server (qwen3.8-27b) through the vendor CLIs ork already spawns, with no new HTTP client and no new dependency. No adj record decides this yet.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
- The local server speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages, so `claude`, `codex` and `grok` can each be pointed at it. It costs nothing per token, has no external rate limit, keeps code on the owner's hardware, and works with no AI provider reachable.
- Limits (owner-stated, not measured here): much weaker than frontier models; slower per request (tens of seconds); about 2 to 4 concurrent requests (owner estimate); one model served at a time; no SLA.
- The `-local` wrappers (`claude-local`, `codex-local`, `grok-local`) are shell functions and config files in the sibling repo (`agents/llmnode/docs/agents.md:22-60`). A headless spawn by ork does not run a shell function. Their source is not in any repo (`agents/llmnode/open-questions.md:33`).
- ork maps only `claude code`, `codex` and `grok` to an adapter (`internal/daemon/runs.go:349`). Matrix row r33 (Agent `Local (vLLM)`, qwen3.8-27b) is added as a candidate and stays "skipped: no adapter" until this slice decides how a local row maps.
- Owner guidance, a judgment and not measured: local suits mechanical edits from a clear spec, test and doc generation for existing code, log and diff summaries, private code, long unattended loops and offline use. Frontier suits planning, hard debugging, large refactors, unfamiliar code and review of local output. Pattern: plan with frontier, execute with local, review with frontier.
- Candidate models, not in the matrix: Qwen3.8-27B 8-bit (listed by vllm-metal, untested); Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B 4-bit (experimental on vllm-metal, untested). Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B is not available locally.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Tests use fake vendor scripts and injected clocks; no live server.

- A matrix row with Agent `claude-local`, `codex-local` or `grok-local` gives a lineup entry with that vendor, model and effort; matrix text prints `used as NAME` (`TestLocalMatrixRowsKeepTheirVendorIdentity`, `TestLocalMatrixUsePrintsTheLauncherName`).
- `supportsVendor` accepts all three local vendors; `vendors set` can mark one out (`TestLocalVendorSupportAndOwnerMarks`). CLI local names pass vendor validation (`TestLocalVendorCommandsAcceptLauncherNames`); doctor reports optional local launchers (`TestLocalDoctorListsOptionalLaunchers`).
- The dispatcher executes each local binary with row model, effort and resume arguments under the existing adapter rules. The grok-local matrix model is latest (ROW-LATEST owner answer), so the existing Grok rule omits -m. ork injects no URL, key or launcher-owned studio-local flag (`TestLocalDispatcherUsesLaunchersAndRowFlags`).
- Local launchers inherit the daemon environment without cloud vendor_env; local fixture candidates keep the local vendor directory (`TestLocalDispatcherDoesNotInheritCloudVendorEnv`, `TestLocalDispatcherSavesFixturesUnderLocalIdentity`).
- A cloud claude out mark does not skip a claude-local row, and the reverse; assert the actual run's role records (`TestLocalAndCloudOutMarksSelectIndependentRows`).
- Four local slots are shared across the three vendors; a fifth waits, and cloud vendor slots remain independent (`TestLocalVendorsShareFourSlots`). Local spec checks share that pool (`TestLocalSpecCheckSharesTheRolePool`).
- Missing launchers are skipped with a reason naming the launcher and PATH, in recommended and explicit chains (`TestLocalMatrixSkipsMissingLauncherWithAReason`, `TestLocalOverrideSkipsMissingLauncherWithAReason`). Repeated unchanged plans keep the same note (`TestLocalMissingLauncherNotesAreStableAcrossPlans`).
- A run whose implementer is local does not wait on a full global/project cap; a frontier run does not wait on a full local pool; a fifth local run waits. Its local reservation lasts through frontier review/gate rounds (adj 192). RESERVED-ONE: local roles in one run use its reserved slot serially. PRIMARY: the admitted plan's first implementer fixes its cap class for the run lifetime (owner answers 2026-11-09). Prove admission, fifth-run queue/release, shared spec-role capacity, review/gate retention, and stable class across fallback.
- A local role past 45 minutes is stopped and falls back despite output; cloud DefaultHungAfter stays 30 minutes of silence (`TestLocalRoleFallsBackAfterFortyFiveMinutesDespiteOutput`, `TestLocalSpecCheckTimeoutFallsBackWithAReport`). Machine sleep does not count toward the 45 minutes (`TestLocalRoleTimeoutIgnoresMachineSleep`).
- Local briefs retain their adapter's permission/skill rules, and run-tree costs display local without dollars (`TestLocalBriefKeepsItsAdapterRules`, `TestLocalRunTreeCostHasNoDollarAmount`).

Unreachable-endpoint classifier and fallback samples remain S303 per the existing owner decision of 2026-11-07. No classifier rule is added in S301.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Owner decisions of 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07 (adj 179 to 181, 183, 186 to 188): cover claude, codex and grok; local rows get their own vendor identity, out mark and slot cap; the cap is one shared pool of 4 across the local vendors (adj 187, which supersedes 182); no role defaults to local; fallback to the next cloud row is automatic when the endpoint is unreachable; one local model at a time.

Launchers (owner, 2026-11-06): `claude-local`, `codex-local` and `grok-local` are shell functions in the owner's `~/.bashrc` today, which a headless spawn cannot run. The owner makes each an executable script on PATH, outside the repo, that sets its own environment and ends by running the CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `grok -m studio-local`). ork spawns the script as a binary and keeps no URL, key or model setting. Adj 183 holds once the scripts exist. The script text, the tailnet host and the key path stay out of the repo.

1. Verify first, on the owner's machine, and record each command and result: `command -v claude-local codex-local grok-local` in the environment the daemon starts with; each launcher run headless with the flags ork passes (`--effort`, `-m`, resume) against the server. Do not assume. If a launcher is still a function, stop and ask.
2. Mapping (adj 188, which supersedes 184 and 185): Agent `claude-local`, `codex-local` and `grok-local` map to the claude, codex and grok adapters with the same name as binary and as lineup vendor. Add the three names to `supportsVendor`. The Agent field stays the key (adj 155). Check that a launcher that already passes `-m` (grok-local passes `-m studio-local`) does not clash with the `-m` ork adds from the row's model.
3. Environment: ork inherits the daemon environment and sets nothing local. Nothing local goes in `projects.json` or `vendor_env`.
4. Caps and marks: one shared local pool across the three local vendors, 4 slots (adj 187); each local vendor has its own out mark. Cloud and local marks are independent.
5. Reasoning and timeouts: check what `--effort` does under the launcher, since `claude-local` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` itself and the server accepts low, medium and xhigh. Check that a reply of tens of seconds, and the 30 minute hung timer (`engine.DefaultHungAfter`), do not classify as a failure.
6. Fallback: classify an unreachable endpoint through the existing adapter classifiers as an error, so adj 156 moves to the next matrix row; if the classifiers do not do that, add the narrowest rule.
7. Update the matrix row r33 to the launcher Agent value with `slicer relay-roles`; local versus frontier stays a matrix row, with no separate ork setting. Update `docs/design.md`, `docs/boundaries.md` and `docs/state.md` to match.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). (1) All three local launchers get matrix rows: claude-local, codex-local and grok-local. (2) A local row is picked first by a matrix condition, size S and well specified; local stays a fallback elsewhere. (3) This slice is S301a. Step 6 (classify an unreachable endpoint and fall back) moves to S303, which needs one captured server-down sample per launcher (adj 23, 77); the "launcher unreachable" failing test above belongs to S303. (4) A cloud vendor_env does not apply to its local twin. (5) Local rows show cost as "local", with no dollar amount. (6) Which roles each local launcher suits is measured in S304, not guessed here. (7) grok-local write roles are S305; until it lands, a grok-local row is read-only roles. Step 7 changes: r33 is one row per launcher (three rows), with the S-and-well-specified condition on the implementer rows; set it with `slicer relay-roles`. Also in scope: add the three names to the CLI `vendorNames`, doctor, the briefs, the runners' `Spec.Bin`, the fixture directories, and the shared pool in `internal/engine/vendors.go`.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview), adj 192 (roles.local-model.cap-exempt). A run whose implementer is a -local row takes a slot in the local pool of 4 (adj 187) for the whole run, its frontier review and gate rounds included, and takes no global or project cap slot. Other runs use the global and project caps as today. With a project cap of 2 and a local pool of 4, two frontier runs and up to four local runs go together. Add failing tests for: a local run does not wait on a full global or project cap; a frontier run does not wait on a full local pool; a fifth local run waits for a local slot. Update docs/design.md (the cap text near lines 245-255) and docs/state.md.

Owner decision (2026-11-09, resumed implementer answer): ROW-LATEST. Set the grok-local matrix row model to latest so the existing Grok adapter omits -m and the launcher selects its configured model. No launcher or adapter argument change. Pass-row-values still applies to claude-local and codex-local (adj 198). Local roles have the 45-minute elapsed fallback limit in S301; cloud roles keep DefaultHungAfter unchanged. Local rows remain fallback-only, size S and well specified, after cloud rows.

Owner answers (2026-11-09, resumed implementer attempt 3): RESERVED-ONE. A local run reserves one shared local slot; its local roles use that reservation one at a time. PRIMARY. The first implementer row in the admitted plan fixes the run cap class for its lifetime, including fallback to another vendor class. Finish adj 192 whole-run reservation and cap exemption with these rules.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `adj check "roles.local-model"`: done when line 1 is `decided`.
- The handoff note lists the output of `command -v claude-local codex-local grok-local` (three paths) and the exit status of each launcher's headless run. If the sandbox cannot reach the server, headless-run evidence becomes a `[HUMAN CHECK]` item for the owner.
- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `slicer check`, `adj lint`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: - Branch and worktree per AGENTS.md; no commit until the owner approves.

sections.heading: Not in this slice
sections.body: No role defaults to local. No second local model at once. No Nemotron or 8-bit Qwen row (untested). Writing or changing the launchers and their key handling (the agents repo). Measuring local quality. A base URL or key setting in ork.
